conceptBreakdown.content:
### 9.1 Comparative Respiratory Pathophysiology Matrix

| Respiratory Disorder | Primary Etiology / Trigger | Pathological Mechanism | Clinical & Diagnostic Manifestations |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Asthma** | Allergic hypersensitivity to environmental allergens (*pollen, dust mites*) | IgE-mediated mast cell degranulation triggering bronchiolar smooth muscle spasms, mucosal edema, and mucus hypersecretion | Difficulty breathing, expiratory **wheezing sounds**, reduced $\text{FEV}_1/\text{FVC}$ ratio. Treated with $\beta_2$-agonists. |
| **Emphysema** | Chronic cigarette smoking or inherited **$\alpha_1$-Antitrypsin Deficiency** | Protease-antiprotease imbalance; neutrophil elastase destroys alveolar septal walls, converting alveoli into large, inelastic sacs | Decreased respiratory surface area, loss of elastic recoil, air trapping (**barrel chest**), reduced diffusion capacity. |
| **Occupational Disorders (Silicosis / Asbestosis)** | Long-term inhalation of silica dust, asbestos fibers, or coal dust in mining | Alveolar macrophages engulf mineral dust, lyse, and release cytokines triggering chronic **Fibrosis** | Proliferation of fibrous connective tissue, irreversible lung scarring, progressive dyspnea, and respiratory failure. |
